lessons.title: Storage principles and types of stores
lessons.html:
The aim of storage

Fruit is stored to hold it in good condition until it is shipped or sold, sometimes for days and, for apples and pears, sometimes for months. Storage slows down the fruit's respiration, water loss, ripening and decay. The main tools are temperature, humidity, air movement and atmosphere.

Storage conditions

  • Temperature: the most important factor. Each fruit kind, cultivar and market protocol has a set temperature. Too warm shortens life; too cold can cause chilling or freezing injury.
  • Relative humidity (RH): high humidity reduces shrivelling and stem drying, but condensation on fruit can encourage decay.
  • Air circulation: cold air must move evenly through all pallets so there are no warm spots.
  • Ethylene control: ethylene gas speeds ripening. Ventilation or scrubbers may be used, and ethylene-producing fruit is kept away from sensitive fruit where required.

Types of stores

StoreUse
Pre-cooler / forced-air coolerRapidly removes field heat by pulling cold air through cartons
Regular cold store (RA)Holds fruit at set temperature and humidity
Controlled atmosphere (CA) storeGas-tight rooms with reduced oxygen and raised carbon dioxide for long-term storage, mainly apples and pears
Dispatch / holding storeShort holding before loading

Controlled atmosphere safety

CA rooms have so little oxygen that a person entering can lose consciousness within moments and die. Only trained, authorised people may open or enter CA rooms, following the permit and gas-testing procedure. Never enter a sealed CA room, even to rescue someone. Raise the alarm instead.

lessons.title: Managing fruit in storage
lessons.html:
Loading the store

  1. Check the room is clean, dry, and at the set temperature before loading.
  2. Check each pallet's card and record its position, so every pallet can be found quickly and traced.
  3. Stack pallets according to the room plan, leaving gaps from walls, between rows and below the evaporator so air can flow. Never block fans or air returns.
  4. Keep different products separate where the plan or protocol requires, for example fruit with different temperature needs.
  5. Load quickly and keep doors closed as much as possible.

Monitoring storage

  • Record air temperatures at set times, and check pulp temperatures of sample fruit in different positions in the room.
  • Check humidity, and on CA rooms the oxygen and carbon dioxide readings, as the procedure requires.
  • Check data logger or monitoring system alarms.
  • Inspect fruit samples regularly for decay, shrivelling, softening, chilling injury and other disorders. Report trends early to the QC manager.
  • Check the room itself: door seals, ice build-up on evaporators, water on the floor, unusual noise from the refrigeration plant.

Stock control

Use the stock system to know what is in each room. Usually fruit is dispatched first in, first out (FIFO), but the QC manager may decide to send fruit with shorter storage potential first. Keep the stock record up to date with every movement in and out. Do stock counts as scheduled and report differences.

Problems and actions

ProblemAction
Temperature outside limitsReport immediately to supervisor and refrigeration technician; record time and readings
Decay increasingInform QC; batches may need to be dispatched sooner or re-packed
Door not sealingReport for repair; minimise openings
Ammonia smellLeave the area, raise the alarm and follow the emergency procedure

Safety

Wear warm clothing, know the inside door release, never allow anyone to be locked in, keep to walkways where forklifts operate, and follow the CA entry rules strictly.

Key points

  • Storage slows respiration, water loss, ripening and decay.
  • Temperature, humidity, air flow and atmosphere must be controlled.
  • Stack for air flow, record pallet positions and keep doors closed.
  • Monitor air and pulp temperatures, fruit condition and stock records.
  • Never enter a controlled atmosphere room unless trained and authorised.

quiz.question: What is the most important factor in fruit storage?
What does a controlled atmosphere (CA) store change?

options.text: It lowers oxygen and raises carbon dioxide

quiz.question: A colleague has collapsed inside a sealed CA room. What should you do?

options.text: Rush in to pull them out
Hold your breath and go in
Raise the alarm and do not enter
Open the door and wait inside

quiz.question: Why must gaps be left between pallets and walls?

options.text: To make room for people to sit
So cold air can flow evenly

quiz.question: Why is each pallet's position recorded?

options.text: So it can be found quickly and traced

quiz.question: Fruit stored too cold can suffer chilling or freezing injury.
If you smell ammonia in the store, you should continue working and report it at the end of the shift.
What should be monitored during storage? (select all that apply)

options.text: Fruit condition such as decay and shrivelling
The weather in the export country
